key_insight: E-prop trained a biologically inspired spiking network to match backpropagation through time at 100% survival, while more biologically faithful schemes performed substantially worse.
engineering_relevance: Biologically inspired spiking controllers offer a potential route to humanoid locomotion, but training choices strongly affect control reliability.
method: Distill a reinforcement learning expert policy using dataset aggregation.
Compare frozen recurrent weights, reward-modulated STDP, e-prop, and backpropagation through time.
Evaluate locomotion survival and demonstrate brief stepping on the Unitree H1-2 humanoid.
evidence_signal: Reported survival rates were 100% for e-prop and backpropagation through time, approximately 43.7% for the fixed reservoir, and approximately 11% for reward-modulated STDP.
watch_item: Brief physical stepping does not establish sustained real-world locomotion robustness or feasibility in living neural cultures.
paper_title: Controlling the Humanoid Robot H1-2 With a Simulated Biologically Plausible Network
